highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.224: Self-Hosted Runners & Archive Plugin Source
highlights.summary: Claude Code now lets Team and Enterprise users turn their own machines or containers into runners for web, mobile, and desktop sessions using `claude self-hosted-runner`. A new `archive` plugin source also lets you install plugins directly from a ZIP file over HTTPS, no git required. These additions give teams much more flexibility in deployment and plugin management.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.221: Focus View in VS Code
highlights.summary: A new Focus View mode has been added to the VS Code extension, which hides verbose tool activity behind a clean per-turn summary with a live running-tool indicator. Toggle it quickly with `Ctrl+Alt+F` or via the Command Palette using 'Claude Code: Toggle Focus view'. This is great for developers who find the tool activity stream distracting during longer agentic tasks.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.222: Worktree Isolation Security Fix
highlights.summary: An important security fix ensures that worktree-isolated sessions and their sub-agents can no longer run destructive git commands against the main checkout. Isolation now properly covers both file edits and Bash commands across every session type. If you use background agents or multi-worktree workflows, upgrading to this version is strongly recommended.

highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has officially announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude family. Developers using Claude Code can expect significantly improved reasoning, coding, and long-context performance when routing tasks through Opus 5. This is a major milestone worth exploring for complex, multi-step coding projects.

highlights.title: Agent Skills for Team Coding Standards in Claude Code
highlights.summary: This open-source project from Tikal demonstrates how to package your team's coding standards as reusable 'agent skills' that can be shared across Claude Code and Codex. It provides a practical pattern for enforcing consistent code style, architecture guidelines, and review checklists without repeating yourself in every prompt. Teams looking to scale AI-assisted development with shared norms should check this out.

highlights.title: 5 Hacks To Use Claude Code So Well It's Almost Unfair
highlights.summary: This YouTube video covers five advanced productivity techniques for getting dramatically more out of Claude Code in your daily workflow. It's aimed at developers who already know the basics and want to level up with smarter prompting, tool configuration, and task delegation strategies. A great watch if you feel like you're only scratching the surface of what Claude Code can do.

highlights.title: Claude Code Tutorial for Non-Coders (YouTube)
highlights.summary: This beginner-focused YouTube tutorial walks through Claude Code from the very start, assuming no prior coding experience. It covers installation, basic prompting, and how to use Claude Code to build and modify real projects step by step. Perfect for designers, product managers, or newcomers who want to start building with AI assistance today.

highlights.title: 9-Minute Claude Code Setup: Installation, Concepts & Real Usage (China-accessible)
highlights.summary: This Bilibili video offers a fast-paced, beginner-friendly guide to installing and understanding Claude Code, specifically tailored for users in mainland China who need a direct connection workaround. In just nine minutes it covers core concepts, real-world usage examples, and practical setup tips. Ideal for Chinese-speaking developers who want to get started quickly without wrestling with access issues.

tips_of_the_day: Use `Ctrl+Alt+F` in VS Code to toggle Focus View and hide noisy tool activity logs — keep it on during long agentic tasks so you can stay focused on the output, not the process.

Before starting a multi-file refactor with background agents, make sure you're on Claude Code v2.1.222 or later — earlier versions had a bug where sub-agents could run destructive git commands against your main branch.

Package your team's coding conventions (naming rules, architecture patterns, PR checklist items) as a shared agent skill file so every developer's Claude Code session automatically follows the same standards without extra prompting.
